record.category: climate reanalysis and forecast archive (token-gated API)

free_tier.stated: Free data, account required: 'If you do not have an account yet, please register ... Once logged in, copy the code displayed below to the file $HOME/.cdsapirc' with url https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/api and a personal access token.
free_tier.notes: No price, no byte allowance and no quota is published on the API setup page.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a retrieval request returns a packaged file (NetCDF, GRIB or ZIP) built from the requested variable, area and period

retention.stated: the archive is the product: ERA5 and the other datasets are reissued, not deleted, and a retrieval result is held for a limited period before it must be re-requested
retention.notes: The result-retention window is not stated on the page read; do not treat this row as a measured value.

egress.terms: Free. The token is identity, not payment.

record.interface_detail: HTTPS API at https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/api with the cdsapi python client; the token goes in $HOME/.cdsapirc. Process listing at /api/retrieve/v1/processes.
record.tooling: cdsapi (pip install 'cdsapi>=0.7.7') is the vendor's own client; curl can drive the same endpoints with the PRIVATE-TOKEN header.
record.chaining: The only free ERA5-class reanalysis source among debrid providers; pair it with a compute sandbox because a full reanalysis pull is tens of GB and needs processing where it lands.

limits.value: no numeric limit published on the setup page; retrievals are queued server-side and the queue position is the observable wait

record.limits_note: The real gate is identity: registration plus a token plus, per dataset, a licence acceptance. The token is a credential and was not created here, so no retrieval was attempted.
record.binding_note: Nothing in the seven-kind vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month that could be measured here; the gate that does fail is identity, which the vocabulary carries in identity_cost rather than in limits.

identity_cost.detail: A CDS account (email registration) plus a personal access token copied into .cdsapirc, plus a licence acceptance per dataset. No card and no institution.

record.reliability_note: Retrievals are queued and can take minutes to hours at peak; a client must poll a request id rather than expect a stream. No rate was measured because no token exists here.
record.confidence_note: The setup page was read and the process listing answered anonymously, which proves the service is live but not that a retrieval works. A retrieval with a real token would move this to measured.

evidence.proved: account registration, personal access token in $HOME/.cdsapirc, cdsapi>=0.7.7, url https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/api
200 with 25,713 bytes of JSON to an anonymous client - the process catalogue is public even though retrieval is not

record.notes: Caveat is the account and the queue, not the price. This is the clearest example in the sector of a resource that is free but not anonymous: the bytes cost nothing and the token is mandatory.

record.provider: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE / ESA DIAS) - 12 TB/month of free READ, zero writable storage

free_tier.stated: 12 TB per rolling 30 days of download via S3/OData/STAC for a Copernicus General User, 20 MB/s per connection, 4 concurrent connections, 2,000 requests/min, empty-account registration. After the transfer limit is hit, bandwidth drops to 1 MB/s and 1 concurrent connection until the 30-day total falls back under the limit. Data Workspace adds 0.1 TB/month of deferred-access transfer and 25 processed products/month. JupyterLab gives 10 GB of persistent scratch, 30-day idle expiry.

egress.terms: The whole quota IS egress - this is the largest free read allowance found anywhere in the programme, but there is no general-purpose bucket to write to.

record.tooling: S3 credentials self-service from the user panel against eodata.dataspace.copernicus.eu; openEO API (10,000 credits/month, temporary boost); Sentinel Hub APIs (10,000 requests/month); s3cmd/boto3 documented.
record.chaining: Per account, and the 30-day rolling window means 12 TB/month sustained without cycling accounts. Creodias resells the same platform with paid extensions.

limits.value: 12 TB of downloads per rolling 30 days
1 MB/s and 1 concurrent connection after the 12 TB limit

record.limits_note: Read-only EO products. No user-owned bucket: the S3 endpoint serves the mission archive. Registration is open to anyone with an email and is self-service.

identity_cost.detail: registration form (required fields not itemised on the page) with email verification

record.reliability_note: CloudFerro-operated for ESA; the 1 MB/s throttle after the cap is a hard cliff, not a soft degrade.
record.confidence_note: the vendor pages of the 2026-11-03 evidence rows were read and captured (https://documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu/Quotas.html, https://documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu/Registration.html); a field that decides the verdict is not cited by those captures, so the rung stays reported
